title: MGMem: An Efficient, Deterministic, and Provenance-Preserving Framework for Long-Horizon Agent Memory
description:
arXiv:2611.33174v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon Large Language Model (LLM) agents need persistent memory that surfaces the right past interaction at the right time across thousands of turns. Many systems index by invoking generative LLMs to rewrite history into summaries, facts, or knowledge graphs--a step that is (a) costly (thousands of generative calls per build), (b) non-deterministic (undermining reproducibility and giving inconsistent answers across runs), and (c) provenance-erasing (the reader sees synthesized text, not the original turn). We propose MGMem, a framework with no generative indexing calls that replaces this step with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline: recurring mentions across sessions are organized into an incidence graph, question mentions are resolved by a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver, and raw dialogue episodes are returned to the reader. On English multi-session dialogue QA, MGMem outperforms matched-protocol baselines on LoCoMo without generative indexing calls; on the full LongMemEval-S, it remains competitive overall and leads or ties on single-session types among local retrieval comparisons. Code: https://github.com/junhong-h/MGMem

title: Beyond Static Charts: Benchmarking Interactive Chart-to-Code Generation for MLLMs
description:
arXiv:2611.31345v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in chart-to-code generation. However, existing benchmarks mainly focus on static charts, overlooking interactive charts that enable richer and more expressive data exploration. Unlike static chart-to-code generation, which emphasizes visual consistency, interactive chart-to-code evaluation targets behavioral consistency, requiring chart states to evolve correctly under sequences of user interactions, thereby rendering traditional one-step evaluation paradigms ineffective. To address this gap, we introduce ChartInt, the first benchmark specifically designed for interactive chart-to-code generation. ChartInt consists of 2,779 carefully annotated examples covering common interaction patterns such as hover, highlight, and tooltips. Additionally, ChartInt incorporates editing tasks such as data updates, style adjustments, and cross-chart style transfer to expand real-world application scenarios. To enable reliable evaluation of interaction behavior, we propose a preset state snapshot protocol that predefines target interaction states and deterministically triggers interaction events, transforming dynamic behaviors into reproducible evaluation targets. Based on this protocol, we design a multi-dimensional evaluation framework measuring semantic and stylistic consistency. Experiments show that while current MLLMs perform well on static charts, their performance drops significantly on interactive tasks, highlighting the need for interaction-aware benchmarks.

title: Engineering a Zero-Backend Multiplayer Party Game with Local-First State
description:
Every weekend, developers rebuild the same CRUD architecture. Auth microservices, WebSockets for real-time room sync, Redis state stores, and Kubernetes clusters just to let three people guess words on a couch. When we set out to build Balaka, our local-first party word game, we asked a radical question: What if we deleted the backend entirely?

If you are building party apps, utilities, or localized tools, throwing away infrastructure often solves scaling, latency, and privacy problems before they even exist. Here is how we engineered a 16-player, multi-deck word game that runs completely disconnected from the internet on a single mobile device.

The Single-Device State Machine Challenge

Traditional multiplayer games rely on a central source of truth. A server arbitrates state, validates moves, and broadcasts deltas back to clients. But when 3 to 16 players crowd around a single phone passing it back and forth, the architecture flips. The device is the cloud.

We modeled the game loop as a deterministic finite state machine (FSM) managed entirely in client memory. Because the phone is handed physically between players, our state manager tracks turn transitions, score multipliers, timer interrupts, and word vocabulary sets without a single network call.

  • Deterministic Transitions: Every phase change—from guessing to explanation to scoring—is an immutable event dispatched locally.
  • Memory Efficiency: 1,750+ localized Ukrainian words, including tech-specific decks like IT & Office Pain, are pre-bundled into a compressed JSON structure loaded instantly into memory on boot.
  • Zero Latency: State rendering operates at native refresh rates because there is no network serialization penalty.

Local-First Storage & Custom Deck Builders

Users love extensibility, which usually means building a cloud database, sync engines, and conflict-resolution algorithms. For our custom deck builder, we bypassed remote databases entirely and utilized local persistent storage paired with a robust schema validation layer.

When a player creates a custom deck of words, the payload is serialized, validated against strict length and character constraints, and written directly to local storage. Because there is no server-side validation or moderation queue, creation happens instantaneously. Players can instantly switch between themed decks—from classic Alias and Taboo mechanics to custom office humor—without waiting for an API response.

Eliminating the Middleman: Zero-Account Onboarding

Modern software forces users through an identity tax: download, sign up with Google, verify email, accept terms, and create a profile. For a casual party game, every second spent on onboarding destroys user momentum.

By operating entirely offline, we eliminated user accounts, OAuth tokens, and session management. The app launches straight into the party menu. There is no database to breach, no telemetry to harvest, and no GDPR compliance overhead for user PII. Privacy isn't just a marketing bullet point; it’s an architectural constraint we enforced by having zero network interfaces.

Lessons from Building Lean Infrastructure

Stepping away from cloud dependencies forced us to rethink how mobile apps are engineered. When you cannot rely on server logs to debug production crashes or remote feature flags to push updates, your client-side code has to be bulletproof.

  • Embrace the Metal: Mobile processors are remarkably powerful. Leveraging local execution keeps user interactions snappy and resource consumption minimal.
  • Keep Bundles Tight: Stripping out heavy networking libraries and analytics SDKs dropped our binary size drastically.
  • Design for the Edge: Offline-first architecture forces you to design for resilience. If your app works in a subway tunnel with zero bars, it will work anywhere.

If you are tired of paying the SaaS tax and maintaining infrastructure for utilities that don't need it, try building closer to the metal. Check out Balaka to see how local-first design handles high-energy group dynamics, or grab it directly on Google Play.

title: November 25, 2026
description:
BigQuery

Feature

You can use cross-cloud connections to query data in AWS, Azure, and Salesforce Data 360 from all BigQuery regions with more feature availability than standard connections that use BigQuery Omni. This feature is generally available (GA).

Deprecated

The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is deprecated and will be shut down on August 31, 2027.

Key milestone dates:

  • Nov 20, 2026: Access to the BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is restricted to projects that recorded active usage between March 1, 2026, and August 31, 2026.
  • August 31, 2027: The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 will be fully shut down. After this date, calls to the v1beta1 endpoint will fail with a NOT_FOUND error.

What you need to do:

To prevent service disruption, migrate your workloads from v1beta1 to the generally available BigQuery Storage API v1. The v1 API is backward-compatible with v1beta1.

  • SDKs and connectors: If you use connectors or client libraries, update them to the latest versions to ensure they default to the v1 API:
    • Simba ODBC/JDBC for BigQuery
    • Google BigQuery ODBC / JDBC driver
    • Trino BigQuery plugin
    • Apache Beam BigQuery connector
    • Spark BigQuery connector
    • Scio BigQuery plugin
  • Custom code: If your applications call the v1beta1 API directly (for example, using gRPC), update your code to target the v1 API endpoint (google.cloud.bigquery.storage.v1).

For more information, see the BigQuery Storage API reference.

If you are using v1beta1 and have concerns with this deprecation schedule, please contact us via a support case.

title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
description:
arXiv:2611.31737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sustained Large Language Model (LLM) inference generates significant heat that exacerbates silicon aging and reduces GPU reliability. Because GPU temperature fluctuates continuously with workload intensity and ambient conditions, keeping it in a safe range requires real-time frequency scaling, which inevitably comes at the cost of either throughput or accuracy. To address this tightly coupled challenge, we propose GreenDynaMix, the first runtime system to jointly integrate a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator. A sensitivity-aware allocator leverages intrinsic importance signals from the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router to assign higher precision to critical experts, preserving accuracy. Experiments on server, desktop, and embedded platforms demonstrate that GreenDynaMix reduces the temperature-induced aging rate of GPUs during LLM inference by 25-33%. Without offline profiling or model retraining, it recovers throughput at a perplexity cost of 0.9-1.6% with 8-bit/4-bit mixed precision, rising to 9.4% where memory forces 4-bit/2-bit.

title: Fail closed on Rapid Security Response, Family Sharing Ask to Buy, and Safety Check
description:
When narrative content drives a physical actuator, three interrupt paths look like "just restore state" until they are not: a Rapid Security Response / "Restart to Finish Installing a Security Response" / "Important Security Response Available" sheet mid-session, a Family Sharing Ask to Buy / "X wants to buy…" / "Approve this purchase" / Screen Time "Ask for More Time" request from a family member, and Safety Check / Emergency Reset / "Reset Sharing & Access" / "Manage Sharing & Access." Each needs a default that fails closed — toward idle, toward re-arm only after a named beat, toward interrupt-clear ≠ motor authority.

on rapid_security_response_or_restart_to_finish_installing_opened():
    ramp_to(IDLE, at=next_beat_boundary)
    armed = false
    on restarted_or_install_later_or_sheet_dismissed():
        # Rapid Security Response UI gone ≠ motor envelope restored
        await user_resume(); await next_named_beat(); arm()

on family_sharing_ask_to_buy_or_ask_for_more_time_opened():
    ramp_to(IDLE, at=next_beat_boundary)
    armed = false
    on request_approved_or_declined_or_dismissed():
        # Family Sharing approval UI cleared ≠ motor authority
        await user_resume(); await next_named_beat(); arm()

on safety_check_or_emergency_reset_or_reset_sharing_and_access_opened():
    ramp_to(IDLE, at=next_beat_boundary)
    armed = false
    on safety_check_completed_or_canceled_or_dismissed():
        # Safety Check / Emergency Reset UI gone ≠ previous intensity restored
        await user_resume(); await next_named_beat(); arm()

The Rapid Security Response rule is easy to mix up with a regular iOS or software-update "restart to finish installing iOS" prompt, a controlling-app update that replaces the process, Stolen Device Protection / Lockdown Mode / Inactivity Reboot, and a compromised-password or data-leak security recommendation. A regular OS-update restart is a full software-update cycle. An app update replaces the controlling process. Stolen Device Protection and Lockdown Mode are device-theft or hardened-mode surfaces. A compromised-password alert is about a leaked saved password. Rapid Security Response is a system mid-cycle security-patch install or restart sheet. Restarting now, installing later, or dismissing that sheet only clears that UI; it must not restore motor authority.

The Ask to Buy / Ask for More Time rule sits next to — but is not — this user's own StoreKit purchase or subscription sheet, an Age Assurance or Confirm Age sheet, this device's own Guided Access or Screen Time app-limit lock, or an Ask App Not to Track prompt. StoreKit is this user's own purchase sheet. Age Assurance is this user's age gate. Guided Access or a Screen Time app limit is a lock on this device. ATT is a tracking-permission prompt. Ask to Buy and "Ask for More Time" are system family-approval cards from another family member. Approving, declining, or dismissing that request only clears that UI; it must not restore motor authority.

The Safety Check rule is a system sharing-review or emergency-reset flow, not an incoming person-to-person "share my location" request, not revoking or re-granting a single app permission, not Find My Play Sound / Lost Mode / Remote Lock, not Stolen Device Protection / Lockdown Mode / Inactivity Reboot, not a Check In or "Are you OK?" prompt, and not an Apple ID new-device or two-factor alert. A location-share request is one person asking to see your location. An OS permission revoke is a single-app entitlement change. Play Sound, Lost Mode, and Remote Lock are Find My device-control actions. Check In is a trip-safety confirmation. An Apple ID new-device alert is an account-login warning. Safety Check and Emergency Reset review or reset sharing and access as a whole. Completing, canceling, or dismissing that flow only clears that interrupt; it must not restore motor authority.

Buyers can test all three without code: dismiss or postpone a Rapid Security Response sheet mid-session and see whether that restarts intensity; approve or decline an Ask to Buy or Ask for More Time card; and finish or cancel Safety Check. The acceptance question is the same in each case: clearing the security-response, family-approval, or sharing-reset UI must not put motor authority back on. These map to questions like "how do AI stories control physical devices" and "Lovense alternative with AI stories."

This is the model CRAVE AI uses for story-controlled play on official devices: AI story-controlled vibrator. Principle write-up: narrative-to-device sync. Devices: AI sex toys.

Disclosure: I work on CRAVE AI. Adults-only product; no explicit content here.

title: Temporal Selective Exploration for Reinforcement Learning-Guided Continuous-Discrete Flow Matching in 3D Molecular Design
description:
arXiv:2611.33417v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow matching has shown strong potential in generative tasks, while its optimization via Reinforcement Learning (RL) remains underexplored, especially in continuous-discrete mixed settings. Moreover, flow matching is formulated as an Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE), whose deterministic trajectories do not naturally support RL optimization. Introducing stochasticity by converting the entire trajectory into a Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) is a common practice. Nevertheless, not all timesteps contribute to the final outcomes, and redundant exploration introduces additional noise. Furthermore, in multi-objective settings, some objectives may dominate the optimization while others receive insufficient updates. In this study, we propose an RL-guided continuous-discrete flow matching framework with temporal selective exploration for 3D de novo molecular design. Specifically, our method jointly optimizes continuous and discrete flow matching for atomic coordinates and molecular identities, respectively, while restricting exploration to timesteps that primarily contribute to target properties, reducing ineffective exploration. We also introduce a reward-based advantage calibration mechanism to mitigate objective dominance in multi-objective optimization. The framework is applied to design inhibitors for both the well-studied target protein EGFR and the challenging Pin1 protein. We identify some novel candidate inhibitors, supported by in silico validation.

title: I Studied 30 Top Apify Actors: Here's How They Price Scrapers (And What I Changed)
description:
I spent a day reading the real pricing data of 30 top-rated Actors on Apify Store. The goal: figure out how successful scrapers charge, so I could reprice my own 12 monitors. Here's what the data actually showed.

1. Almost nobody uses flat "per result" pricing anymore

29 of the 30 actors I checked use PAY_PER_EVENT, not the old flat per-dataset-item model. Apify's own docs confirm PRICE_PER_DATASET_ITEM is no longer supported for new records.

The top actors split charges into multiple named events:

  • apify/instagram-scraper: one result event, $0.0027 per item at FREE tier
  • compass/crawler-google-places: place-scraped, filter-applied, lead-scraped (lead at $0.10 — deliberately expensive to discourage abuse)
  • apify/google-search-scraper: AI add-on events priced at $0.20 on FREE but $0.001–0.009 on GOLD

2. The discount tiers are real — and steep

Every high-rated actor I checked has tiered pricing (eventTieredPricingUsd), not a flat price:

Actor FREE GOLD Drop
instagram-scraper $0.0027 $0.0015 -44%
google-places $0.004 $0.0015 -62%
facebook-posts $0.005 $0.002 -60%

Apify's official quality-score docs literally say: "Consider offering discounts for Bronze, Silver, and Gold subscription tiers — these incentives can increase your Actor's adoption among engaged customers."

3. What I changed

My 12 monitors were all priced flat. I migrated every one to tiered PPE pricing (FREE full price → GOLD 50%) using the eventTieredPricingUsd field, which is mutually exclusive with the flat eventPriceUsd.

One gotcha: the API rejects a pricing change unless you submit the full history of pricing objects first, then append exactly one new object. For two actors with long histories, the SDK call timed out but the write had actually succeeded — always re-read the actor before retrying.

4. Other quality-score details I fixed

  • Example input: every one of my actors had the template default {"helloWorld": 123}. Users clicking "Try it" saw garbage. Replaced with real inputs like {"query": "CRISPR"}.
  • README structure: Apify recommends Introduction / Tutorial / Pricing / Use cases / FAQ, 300+ words. Mine were 150–250 words with no Use cases section.
  • Automated testing: Apify runs your actor daily with the schema's prefill values and requires a non-empty dataset within 5 minutes. One of my actors had a required input with no prefill — it would have been flagged "Under maintenance".

Takeaway

If you publish on Apify: the pricing model and the metadata are not "set and forget" — they're ranking signals. Tiered PPE + real example inputs + a proper README cost a few hours and may be worth more than another feature.

Happy to answer questions about the pricing migration in the comments.

title: ArtLang-4D: Articulation-Aware Dynamic Language Fields from Monocular Videos
description:
arXiv:2611.33511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language that describes an articulated object is often about its state: the drawer pulled out the furthest, the door opened halfway, push the drawer all the way in. Existing 3D language fields attach one feature to each point and cannot tell these descriptions apart, and 4D language fields condition on video time, which has no kinematic meaning and cannot be set by a user. We present ArtLang-4D, which reconstructs an articulated object from a single monocular RGB-D video and equips it with a dynamic language field indexed by articulation time t, the normalized state of its joints, instead of video time. The geometry is a canonical triangle field whose triangles follow typed screw joints, discovered from the video without any joint initialization. The language field is supervised by a t-tagged caption bank that describes each part with comparative state phrases in a whitened open-vocabulary text space. A free-form query is answered by maximizing part relevance jointly over parts and states, which returns both the part and the articulation state it describes; a command is then executed by moving only that part along its recovered joint. On the 100 objects of Articulate-100, ArtLang-4D recovers more accurate joints and part geometry than reconstruction and articulation baselines, retrieves the queried state far more reliably than a state-agnostic language field, and executes language commands with lower motion error.

title: Amortizing Exact Orthogonality: Drift-Triggered Restoration for Orthogonal Fine-Tuning
description:
arXiv:2611.33589v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Orthogonal finetuning (OFT) adapts a pretrained weight by an orthogonal transform and preserves its singular values and row angles, but existing methods construct an exact or approximate orthogonal transform at every optimization step. We measure how far a transform $A$ is from orthogonal by its orthogonality defect $\|A^\top A-I\|_2$. For OFTv2, which truncates a Cayley-Neumann series, we show that the truncation order does not determine the defect. At its default order, block defects in checkpoints from the reference implementation span five orders of magnitude. We propose Restarted Tangent Orthogonal Finetuning (RTOFT), which uses the first-order update $W(I+S)$ of a weight $W$ with a skew-symmetric $S$ and restores exact orthogonality by a polar decomposition only when the drift $\|S\|_2$ reaches a tolerance $\tau$. The defect of $I+S$ is exactly $\|S\|_2^2$. Therefore, reading the drift after every update and restoring before the next forward pass guarantees a defect of at most $\tau^2$ in every forward pass, independently of the loss, data, model, and optimizer. A final restoration makes the returned transform exactly orthogonal. On GLUE, RTOFT reduces the training time of block-diagonal, subspace, and butterfly parameterizations from $1.10$-$1.58\times$ to $0.97$-$1.13\times$ that of LoRA, and its block-diagonal version exceeds LoRA by $1.98\pm0.39$ points on the six-task average over five seeds. At $\tau=0.10$, the largest drift read during training stays between $0.10$ and $0.12$ across DeBERTaV3, Qwen, and diffusion models, whereas it ranges from $0.17$ to $1.65$ when restoring once per epoch. In all seven settings of our ablation, the tangent update is worse without restoration than with it, and restoring after every step yields no measurable accuracy gain over restoring at the tolerance and costs $4.5$-$27.5\%$ more per step.

title: I Built AI Test Automation. Today, I Went Back to Manual Testing.
description:
Today, I manually tested a project.

It doesn't sound like anything special.

After all, I've been working in software testing for 16 years. Manual testing used to be a big part of my everyday work. But recently, the way I work has changed quite a bit.

I've built an AI-powered test automation framework at my company, and quite a few projects are now being tested by AI.

From understanding requirements and designing test scenarios to interacting with applications, exploring edge cases, organizing test results, and reporting bugs, AI can now handle many tasks that used to take QA engineers a lot of time.

I know what this framework can do. I've watched it gradually change the way our team works.

So today, when I opened a project and started clicking through the screens, checking things one by one, and looking for problems myself, I found myself thinking about something I hadn't expected.

A Very Simple Bug Report

I found a few issues today and submitted them to our bug tracking system as usual.

But compared with the reports generated by AI, mine were pretty basic.

AI usually produces much more detailed reports. It can organize the testing context, list reproduction steps, describe expected and actual results, attach relevant screenshots and page information, and sometimes even provide an initial analysis of what might have gone wrong.

My reports today were much simpler.

A straightforward title, a few reproduction steps, and a description of what actually happened. A screenshot when necessary.

No lengthy analysis. No particularly elaborate structure.

Just ordinary bug reports.

But the problems were real, and someone still needed to find them and report them.

It suddenly occurred to me that I'd become so used to AI making test results more complete and detailed that seeing my own simple reports today made me think of all the QA engineers who still spend their days finding problems one by one.

Please Appreciate the QA Engineers Who Still Test by Hand

I'm not trying to bring back manual testing.

Quite the opposite. I've been pushing for AI test automation, and I hope more repetitive and time-consuming testing tasks can be handed over to AI.

I know how much efficiency automation can bring.

But today, I suddenly wanted to say something to developers:

Please appreciate the QA engineers who are still testing by hand.

When they submit a bug report, it may not be as detailed as one written by AI. The reproduction steps may not look as polished, and the analysis may not be as complete.

But don't underestimate the time and effort behind finding that issue just because the report looks simple.

What you see might be only a title and a few steps to reproduce the problem.

Before submitting it, the QA engineer may have already tried many things, switched between pages and test data, and explored different paths before confirming that the issue was worth reporting.

Sometimes, finding a seemingly simple bug isn't simple at all.

If the description isn't clear enough, ask the QA engineer for more details. If you can't reproduce it, work together to figure out what's happening.

That's what collaboration between development and QA should look like.

Don't let a simple bug report become a reason to take someone's work less seriously.

AI Will Change Testing, But It Shouldn't Change How We Treat People

I believe more and more projects will adopt AI-powered test automation.

Maybe one day, most routine testing will no longer need to be performed manually by QA engineers.

I hope that day comes, too.

But until then, there are still plenty of QA engineers opening pages by hand, entering data, clicking buttons, and checking results. They may not have sophisticated automation tools or beautiful reports generated by AI. They simply rely on their experience and patience to check, again and again, whether the product works as expected.

Their work may not look exciting, and it may never make it into a company's AI transformation presentation.

But they're still taking responsibility for product quality.

Technological progress should never be a reason to overlook the people who are doing their jobs with care.

Today, while submitting those simple bug reports, I found myself thinking about all the QA engineers who are still doing manual testing.

I'll keep pushing AI test automation and finding more ways to let AI handle testing work.

I just hope that the next time a developer receives a bug report from someone doing manual testing, they'll show a little more patience and understanding.

After all, until AI takes over all the testing, there's still someone sitting in front of a screen, clicking through the application and checking things again and again.

That person deserves to be seen.

And deserves to be treated with respect.

title: Erreurs d’e-mail Cloudflare : E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED, E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED et 429 résolues
description:
Les erreurs Cloudflare Email ont commencé à apparaître dans beaucoup plus de logs le 24 novembre 2026, lorsque Cloudflare a rendu l'envoi d'e-mails disponible sur le plan Workers Free. Le piège tient en une ligne du changelog : sur Free, vous ne pouvez envoyer qu'à des adresses de destination vérifiées dans votre propre compte.

Essayez Apidog aujourd'hui

Réponse rapide : E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED signifie que vous êtes sur Workers Free et que le destinataire n'est pas une adresse de destination vérifiée : vérifiez-la ou passez à Workers Paid, et ne réessayez jamais. E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (binding Workers), HTTP 429 (API REST) et 451 4.7.1 (SMTP) signifient que vous avez atteint la limite d'envoi quotidienne de votre compte : mettez le message en file d'attente et réessayez plus tard, ou demandez une limite plus élevée.

Ce que signifient les erreurs Cloudflare Email

Cloudflare Email Service signale un même problème de trois façons : le binding Workers lève une chaîne code, l'API REST renvoie un statut HTTP accompagné d'un code numérique, et SMTP répond avec un code de réponse. Les trois partagent le même ensemble de limites de compte.

Problème Binding Workers API REST SMTP Réessayer ?
Destinataire non autorisé sur votre plan E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED 403, code 10208 550 5.7.1 au moment du RCPT TO Non
Limite d'envoi quotidienne atteinte E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED 429 451 4.7.1 Plus tard
Limite de débit ou de concurrence d'envoi E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED 429, code 10004 451 4.7.1 Oui, avec backoff
Destinataire sur la liste de suppression E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED 400 Message rejeté Non
Compte suspendu pour réputation E_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED 403, code 10207 Non listé Non

Sources : la page Limits de Cloudflare, les codes d'erreur de l'API Workers et les codes de réponse SMTP, consultés le 26 novembre 2026.

Le point clé : le tableau des erreurs REST ne liste qu'une seule entrée 429, 10004 (email.sending.error.throttled), et SMTP utilise 451 4.7.1 à la fois pour la limite de débit et pour la limite quotidienne. Seul le binding vous indique quelle limite vous avez atteinte.

Corriger E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED sur Workers Free

E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED relève d'une règle de plan, pas d'une défaillance passagère. Sur Workers Free, l'envoi d'e-mails n'accepte que les adresses de destination vérifiées dans votre compte. Toute autre adresse échoue de la même manière à chaque tentative, donc ne la réessayez jamais.

Trois solutions s'offrent à vous :

  1. Vérifier l'adresse. Dans le tableau de bord, allez dans Compute > Email Service > Email Routing > Destination Addresses, ajoutez l'adresse et cliquez sur le lien dans l'e-mail de vérification envoyé par Cloudflare. Un compte peut contenir 200 adresses de destination.
  2. Passer à Workers Paid. Le plan payant envoie à n'importe quel destinataire, avec 3 000 e-mails par mois inclus et 0,35 $ par tranche de 1 000 ensuite, selon la page de tarification d'Email Service.
  3. Garder Free pour le courrier interne. Les alertes et rapports destinés à votre propre équipe conviennent au plan Free, et les envois vers des adresses vérifiées échappent aux quotas et aux limites quotidiennes sur tous les plans.

En SMTP, la même règle se manifeste plus tôt dans la session. Cloudflare refuse le RCPT TO non vérifié avec 550 5.7.1. Si votre client envoie ensuite DATA malgré tout, l'intégralité du message échoue avec 554 5.7.1 et aucun destinataire ne le reçoit, y compris les destinataires vérifiés. Séparez les listes de destinataires mixtes avant l'envoi.

Ne la confondez pas avec E_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED, qui provient du paramètre allowed_destination_addresses de votre propre binding.

Corriger E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, HTTP 429 et 451 4.7.1

Les nouveaux comptes démarrent avec un quota quotidien prudent qui augmente selon votre comportement d'envoi, votre délivrabilité et la situation de votre compte. Cloudflare ne publie pas la valeur de départ, et l'ajuste par compte.

Considérez une limite quotidienne comme un « pas aujourd'hui ». Des tentatives rapides ne la débloqueront pas. À la place :

  • Placez le message dans une file d'attente ou une table avec un timestamp not_before à quelques heures de là.
  • Privilégiez le courrier transactionnel (réinitialisations de mot de passe, reçus) par rapport au courrier en masse au retour de la capacité.
  • Si vous avez besoin de plus de marge, utilisez le formulaire « Need a higher limit? » en bas de la page Limits.

Une limite de débit, c'est différent : elle est de courte durée, donc le backoff exponentiel avec jitter est l'outil adapté. Notre guide sur les tentatives avec backoff exponentiel couvre les calculs, et HTTP 429 Too Many Requests explique le code de statut lui-même.

Gérer les erreurs dans un Worker

Le binding vous donne le signal le plus clair, alors branchez sur error.code. Ce Worker ne réessaie que la limite de débit, différe la limite quotidienne et échoue immédiatement sur tout ce qui est permanent :

const PERMANENT = new Set([
  "E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED", "E_RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED",
  "E_RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED", "E_VALIDATION_ERROR", "E_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED",
]);

async function sendEmail(env: Env, msg: EmailMessageBuilder) {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 4; attempt++) {
    try {
      return { status: "sent", id: (await env.EMAIL.send(msg)).messageId };
    } catch (err: any) {
      if (err instanceof TypeError) return { status: "bad_input", reason: err.message };
      if (err.code === "E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED") return { status: "defer" };
      if (PERMANENT.has(err.code)) return { status: "failed", reason: err.code };
      if (err.code !== "E_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" && err.code !== "E_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR") throw err;
      const wait = 2 ** attempt * 500 + Math.random() * 250;
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, wait));
    }
  }
  return { status: "defer" };
}

Le binding tient sur une ligne dans wrangler.jsonc : "send_email": [{ "name": "EMAIL" }]. Une TypeError sans code signifie que l'argument de votre send() ne correspond pas à l'interface (pas de destinataire, ou un EmailAddress sans name) : un bug à corriger, pas un envoi à réessayer.

Gérer un 429 de l'API REST

L'endpoint REST est POST https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send avec un token API Bearer. Les erreurs reviennent dans l'enveloppe standard de Cloudflare, lisez donc errors[0].code :

const BASE = process.env.CF_API_BASE ?? "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4";

async function sendViaRest(accountId, token, payload, attempt = 0) {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/accounts/${accountId}/email/sending/send`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify(payload),
  });
  const body = await res.json();
  if (body.success) return { status: "sent", id: body.result.message_id };

  const code = body.errors?.[0]?.code;
  if (res.status === 403 && code === 10208) return { status: "failed", reason: "recipient_plan_restricted" };
  if (res.status === 429 || res.status >= 500) {
    if (attempt >= 3) return { status: "defer" };
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2 ** attempt * 1000 + Math.random() * 500));
    return sendViaRest(accountId, token, payload, attempt + 1);
  }
  return { status: "failed", reason: `${res.status}:${code}` };
}

Comme un 429 REST peut correspondre à l'une ou l'autre des limites, plafonnez les tentatives et confiez le message à votre file d'attente après la dernière. La variable configurable CF_API_BASE compte plus tard, quand vous pointerez ce client vers un mock.

Vérifiez aussi le corps de la réponse de succès. Avec l'option Drop suppressed recipients activée, un 200 peut tout de même lister des adresses dans suppressed_recipients ou permanent_bounces, et ces destinataires n'ont rien reçu.

Gérer 451 4.7.1 et 550 5.7.1 en SMTP

L'envoi SMTP de Cloudflare passe par smtp.mx.cloudflare.net, port 465, TLS implicite uniquement. Le nom d'utilisateur est la chaîne littérale api_token et le mot de passe est un token API avec la permission Email Sending: Edit. Le port 587 avec STARTTLS n'est pas pris en charge.

Avec Nodemailer, le code de réponse arrive sur err.responseCode :

import nodemailer from "nodemailer";

const transport = nodemailer.createTransport({
  host: "smtp.mx.cloudflare.net", port: 465, secure: true,
  auth: { user: "api_token", pass: process.env.CF_EMAIL_TOKEN },
});

try {
  await transport.sendMail({ from: "alerts@yourdomain.com", to, subject, text });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.responseCode === 451 || err.responseCode === 421) scheduleRetry(); // temporary
  else if (err.responseCode === 550 || err.responseCode === 554) markFailed(err.response);
  else throw err;
}

Une réponse 4xx est temporaire ; une 5xx est permanente. 535 5.7.8 correspond à un nom d'utilisateur ou un token invalide, et 550 5.7.1 Sender denied signifie que le domaine du MAIL FROM n'est pas rattaché au compte du token.

Quand réessayer et quand arrêter

La décision se résume à une question : la même requête réussira-t-elle plus tard sans que vous changiez quoi que ce soit ?

Les erreurs de suppression méritent votre attention. Cloudflare supprime une adresse après des rebonds définitifs (7 jours, ou sans expiration lorsque la boîte n'existe pas), des rebonds temporaires (24 heures par défaut) et des plaintes pour spam validées (sans expiration). Selon la documentation sur la liste de suppression, les envois supprimés ne sont pas décomptés du quota et apparaissent comme Rejected dans les logs. Ne réessayez pas, et ne supprimez pas une suppression liée à une plainte avant que la personne ne se réinscrive.

Vous cherchez encore un fournisseur ? Consultez notre sélection d'API d'e-mail gratuites.

Tester les chemins d'erreur avec Apidog CLI depuis votre agent de codage

Les branches d'erreur sont les moins testées, car un vrai 429 est difficile à déclencher et une vraie limite quotidienne coûte une journée. Laissez plutôt votre agent de codage construire les cas d'échec avec Apidog CLI : des attentes de mock renvoient les corps d'erreur exacts de Cloudflare, et votre client s'exécute contre ceux-ci.

Installez le CLI et le skill de l'agent une seule fois :

npm install -g apidog-cli@latest
apidog login --with-token <YOUR_TOKEN>
npx -y skills add https://apidog.com   # pick your agent when prompted

Donnez ensuite un seul prompt à votre agent :

In Apidog project <id>, add Cloudflare's POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send
endpoint with 200, 403 and 429 responses. Create mock expectations: when the body "to"
is stranger@example.com, return 403 with errors[0].code 10208; when header X-Scenario is
throttle, return 429 with errors[0].code 10004. Then list the endpoint and its mocks.

L'agent trouve l'endpoint, lit le schéma de payload, valide son JSON et écrit les mocks :

apidog endpoint list --project <id> --method POST
apidog cli-schema get mock-create
apidog cli-schema validate mock-create --file mock-403.json
apidog mock create --project <id> --file mock-403.json
apidog mock list --project <id>

Pointez CF_API_BASE vers l'URL de mock du projet, affichée sur l'endpoint dans Apidog, et lancez les tests de votre client REST. Le cas 403 doit renvoyer recipient_plan_restricted sans aucune tentative, et le cas throttle doit réessayer trois fois puis différer. Une fois l'endpoint réel raccordé, l'agent peut créer des cas de test et les exécuter avec apidog run --test-case <caseId> --project <id> -e <envId> -r cli,junit. Le guide Apidog CLI dans Claude Code détaille cette boucle.

Une fois ces exécutions d'agent intégrées à votre semaine, Sharkly permet à votre équipe de les distribuer comme des tâches sur un tableau : chaque agent de codage, Claude Code ou Codex inclus, s'exécute sur votre propre ordinateur avec votre propre plan, et vous validez ce qu'il livre avant la fusion. C'est gratuit pour commencer.

Pour conclure

Ces erreurs appellent des réponses opposées. E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED est définitive tant que vous n'avez pas vérifié l'adresse ou basculé vers Workers Paid, alors échouez vite. E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 429 et 451 4.7.1 relèvent du volume, alors différez et réessayez plus tard. Testez les deux chemins avant votre premier envoi réel.

FAQ

L'envoi d'e-mails Cloudflare fonctionne-t-il sur le plan Workers Free ? Oui, depuis le 24 novembre 2026, mais uniquement vers des adresses de destination vérifiées dans votre compte. Envoyer à quelqu'un d'autre nécessite Workers Paid.

Combien d'e-mails puis-je envoyer par jour ? Cloudflare ne publie pas de chiffre fixe. Les nouveaux comptes démarrent avec une limite quotidienne prudente qui augmente avec la réputation, et vous pouvez demander une augmentation via le formulaire de la page Limits.

Les envois vers des adresses vérifiées sont-ils décomptés de mon quota ? Non. Les envois vers des adresses de destination vérifiées sont gratuits sur tous les plans et ne sont décomptés ni du quota mensuel ni des limites d'envoi quotidiennes.

Dois-je réessayer un 429 de l'API REST Cloudflare Email ? Oui, quelques fois avec un backoff exponentiel et du jitter. Si cela persiste, considérez que vous avez atteint la limite quotidienne et déplacez le message vers une file d'attente différée.

Pourquoi mon envoi SMTP a-t-il échoué avec 554 5.7.1 ? Un destinataire a été refusé au moment du RCPT TO avec 550 5.7.1, généralement une adresse non vérifiée sur Workers Free, et votre client a envoyé DATA malgré tout. Cloudflare rejette alors l'intégralité du message.

title: dxsrc’s Global RSS Feed Is Now a Paid Feature
description:
TL;DR: Access to dxsrc’s main feed—which features some exclusive content—now requires becoming a dxsrc supporter.

Over the years, dxsrc has become one of the leading sources of frontend development news and tools. dxsrc’s growing archives provide unique access to the history of the wider field of web development.

Providing this service for free is not sustainable, however. Book sales pay for some of the work, but so far, few people acknowledge dxsrc’s value by supporting the project on Open Collective.

Starting today, the global RSS feed (with the 250 newest articles and videos) is a paid feature.

You can secure access by a monthly or yearly contribution.

If you don’t like to support dxsrc, you can still follow dxsrc’s individual topic feeds as well as dxsrc’s social media accounts on Mastodon and Bluesky. These are less convenient and reliable but still workable options to stay up-to-date.

Also, if you want to support dxsrc in a different manner and so that the main feed may be made free again, consider buying dxsrc’s books or contributing to the project on Open Collective. You’re not alone: We do the same for the projects we use and like. Thank you.

title: Cloudflare Email Service vs Resend: comparação de preços, limites e API
description:
Cloudflare Email Service vs Resend se resume a duas perguntas: para quem você precisa enviar e-mails e quantas mensagens envia por mês. No plano Workers Free, a Cloudflare só envia para endereços de destino verificados na sua própria conta, ou seja, é um canal gratuito de alertas para a sua equipe, não uma forma gratuita de enviar e-mails para clientes. O plano Free da Resend envia para qualquer pessoa, com limite de 3.000 por mês e 100 por dia. Para envios em produção, a Cloudflare cobra US$ 0,35 por 1.000 e-mails após os 3.000 incluídos no Workers Paid (mínimo de US$ 5 por mês), enquanto a Resend começa em US$ 20 por mês para 50.000.

Experimente o Apidog hoje

A Cloudflare trouxe o Email Sending para o plano Workers Free em 24 de novembro de 2026, e uma resposta ao anúncio resumiu as letras miúdas: "Para Destinatários Verificados*, não para todos." Este guia compara os dois serviços com base nas páginas oficiais de preços, limites e API, consultadas em 26 de novembro de 2026.

Cloudflare Email Service vs Resend em resumo

Cloudflare Email Service Resend
Destinatários no plano Free Apenas endereços de destino verificados na sua conta Qualquer pessoa
Volume no plano Free Ilimitado para endereços verificados 3.000 por mês, 100 por dia
Porta de entrada paga Workers Paid, mínimo de US$ 5 por mês, 3.000 e-mails incluídos Pro, US$ 20 por mês para 50.000 e-mails
Excedente US$ 0,35 por 1.000 US$ 0,90 por 1.000 no Pro, caindo para US$ 0,46 no maior plano Scale
Limite diário Começa conservador para novas contas e cresce conforme a reputação 100 no Free, nenhum nos planos pagos
Interfaces Binding do Workers, API REST, SMTP API REST, SMTP, SDKs oficiais
Destinatários por mensagem 50 (to, cc, bcc somados) 50
Eventos Publicados em uma Cloudflare Queue Webhooks para o seu endpoint HTTPS
Domínio Precisa ser um domínio na sua conta Cloudflare Qualquer provedor de DNS
E-mail de marketing Não coberto pelo Email Sending Broadcasts, com preço por contatos

O que mudou em 24 de novembro

O post de changelog da Cloudflare informa que contas no plano Workers Free agora podem cadastrar domínios de envio e enviar e-mails para seus endereços de destino verificados sem custo. Você pode usar o binding do Workers, a API REST ou SMTP.

Três detalhes importam:

  1. Os destinatários são restritos. Se você enviar para um endereço que não esteja verificado em uma conta Free, o binding lança E_RECIPIENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED.
  2. Envios verificados são gratuitos em todos os planos. Em qualquer plano, mensagens para endereços de destino verificados não contam para a cota mensal nem para os limites diários.
  3. Os envios verificados mudaram de produto. Antes eram um recurso do Email Routing; agora são tráfego do Email Sending, com log de Atividades, analytics, eventos e um novo campo GraphQL isVerifiedRecipient.

Portanto, o plano Free serve para alertas de plantão e relatórios noturnos para a sua própria equipe. Redefinição de senha e recibos vão para desconhecidos, e esses casos exigem o Workers Paid.

Cloudflare Email Service vs Resend: preços

Veja quanto cada serviço cobra em volumes mensais comuns, calculado a partir das duas páginas oficiais (preços da Cloudflare, preços da Resend). O valor da Cloudflare inclui o mínimo de US$ 5 do Workers Paid, que também cobre seu uso do Workers.

E-mails por mês Cloudflare (Workers Paid) Resend
3.000 US$ 5,00 US$ 0 (Free, se você ficar abaixo de 100 por dia)
10.000 US$ 7,45 US$ 20 (Pro)
50.000 US$ 21,45 US$ 20 (Pro)
100.000 US$ 38,95 US$ 35 (Pro)
500.000 US$ 178,95 US$ 350 (Scale)
1.000.000 US$ 353,95 US$ 650 (Scale)

A conta da Cloudflare é simples: subtraia os 3.000 e-mails incluídos e multiplique o restante por US$ 0,35 a cada 1.000. Em 100.000 e-mails, isso dá 97 × US$ 0,35 = US$ 33,95, mais US$ 5.

Abaixo de 3.000 por mês, o Resend Free não custa nada se nenhum dia passar de 100. Exatamente nas faixas de 50.000 e 100.000 da Resend, a Resend é um pouco mais barata. Entre faixas e em volumes altos, a tarifa fixa da Cloudflare vence: cerca de US$ 300 por mês mais barata em 1 milhão de e-mails.

Observações de cobrança: a Cloudflare conta hard bounces na cota, mas não os envios rejeitados na borda da API, como endereços suprimidos. A Resend cobra apenas mensalmente, e os excedentes exigem a opção "Transactional Overages" ativada; caso contrário, você é solicitado a fazer upgrade.

Se você também envia newsletters, a Resend precifica marketing separadamente: os Broadcasts são limitados por contatos, não por e-mails, começando com 1.000 contatos no Free e US$ 40 por mês para 5.000. As páginas do Email Sending da Cloudflare descrevem apenas envio transacional, então compare esse item apenas na Resend.

Limites de envio e de taxa

Cloudflare não publica um número diário fixo. Novas contas "começam com uma cota diária conservadora" que cresce conforme seu comportamento de envio, entregabilidade e histórico da conta (página de limites). Ao atingi-la, cada interface falha à sua maneira:

Interface Resposta ao atingir o limite diário
Binding do Workers E_DAILY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
API REST HTTP 429
SMTP 451 4.7.1 ao final de DATA

Por mensagem: 50 destinatários, 25 MiB no total e 16 KB de cabeçalhos personalizados. Um formulário na página de limites solicita um limite maior.

Resend publica seus números. O Free limita a 100 e-mails por dia, os planos pagos não têm limite diário, e a API permite 10 requisições por segundo por equipe em todos os planos (limites de uso). Uma chamada em lote envia até 100 e-mails como uma única requisição, e cabeçalhos retry-after indicam ao seu cliente quando recuar.

Assim, em uma conta Cloudflare nova, espere que picos de lançamento atinjam um limite que você não consegue ver de antemão, e trate as três formas de erro. Na Resend, planeje em torno de 10 requisições por segundo.

Formato da API e dos SDKs

Ambas as APIs aceitam os mesmos campos principais, então a migração é basicamente um localizar e substituir.

Dentro de um Worker, a Cloudflare oferece um binding. Adicione-o à sua configuração do Wrangler:

[[send_email]]
name = "EMAIL"

Depois, envie a partir do seu handler:

await env.EMAIL.send({
  from: "alerts@yourdomain.com",
  to: "oncall@example.com",
  subject: "Disk usage above 90%",
  text: "Disk usage on db-1 is above 90%.",
});

Fora do Workers, você faz um POST com os mesmos campos para /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send na API REST da Cloudflare usando um token de API, ou usa os SDKs oficiais para Node, Python e Go. O SDK Node da Resend é assim:

import { Resend } from "resend";
const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY);

const { data, error } = await resend.emails.send({
  from: "Acme <welcome@yourdomain.com>",
  to: ["user@example.com"],
  subject: "Welcome",
  html: "<strong>Thanks for signing up.</strong>",
});

A Resend acrescenta idempotencyKey, envios agendados, envio em lote e templates do React Email. Nosso guia da API da Resend percorre cada um deles, e o guia da chave de API da Resend cobre o escopo das chaves. Se preferir controlar pelo terminal, veja como instalar e usar a CLI da Resend.

Eventos e webhooks

Cloudflare publica eventos de Email Sending via event subscriptions em uma Cloudflare Queue. Você a consome com um Worker ou com um consumidor HTTP pull. Cada assinatura cobre um domínio de envio. Os eventos são message.delivered, message.deferred, message.bounced, message.failed, message.rejected e message.complained. A lista não inclui eventos de abertura ou clique.

Resend envia webhooks assinados para o seu endpoint HTTPS. Os eventos incluem email.sent, email.delivered, email.delivery_delayed, email.bounced, email.complained, email.opened, email.clicked, email.failed, email.suppressed e email.received. O plano Free permite 1 endpoint de webhook, o Pro 5 e o Scale 10.

Precisa de rastreamento de abertura e clique? A Resend tem em todos os planos. Já está no Workers? Um consumidor de Queue economiza uma rota pública de webhook.

Configuração de domínio

Cloudflare cadastra um domínio da sua conta Cloudflare e escreve os registros DNS por você: registros MX e SPF em um subdomínio cf-bounce para tratamento de bounces, um registro DKIM e um registro DMARC em _dmarc. Se o seu DNS estiver em outro lugar, você precisaria mover a zona para a Cloudflare primeiro.

Resend funciona com qualquer provedor de DNS: você adiciona os registros SPF e DKIM que ela fornece. O Free inclui 3 domínios, o Pro 10 e o Scale 1.000, com mais 100 por US$ 20 por mês no Pro e no Scale.

Qual escolher?

  • Alertas e relatórios para a sua própria equipe, orçamento de US$ 0: Cloudflare no Workers Free. Verifique o endereço de cada colega, e os envios são gratuitos sem cota.
  • Um projeto paralelo enviando e-mails para usuários reais abaixo de 100 por dia: Resend Free.
  • Um app já no Workers, enviando 200.000 ou mais por mês: Cloudflare no Workers Paid. A tarifa por mensagem é cerca de metade da da Resend nesse volume.
  • Você precisa de rastreamento de abertura e clique, agendamento, React Email ou Broadcasts de marketing: Resend.
  • Seu DNS não está na Cloudflare e você não quer mover: Resend.

Algumas equipes usam os dois: Cloudflare para e-mails internos, Resend para clientes. Nossa coletânea de APIs de e-mail gratuitas lista outras opções.

Teste as duas APIs de envio com o Apidog CLI

Antes de trocar de provedor, teste ambos com as mesmas requisições, incluindo o que seu código faz em um 429. Seu agente de programação pode fazer isso com o Apidog CLI enquanto você revisa o resultado.

Configure uma vez:

npm install -g apidog-cli@latest
apidog login --with-token <YOUR_TOKEN>
npx -y skills add https://apidog.com   # pick your agent when prompted

Em seguida, dê ao Claude Code, Codex ou OpenCode um único prompt:

Write email-providers.yaml, an OpenAPI 3.1 file describing Cloudflare's
POST /accounts/{account_id}/email/sending/send and Resend's POST /emails,
including their 429 responses. Import it into Apidog project <projectId>,
list the endpoints, pick the environment for staging, then run test
scenario <scenarioId> with both keys passed as env vars and tell me which
provider was slower and whether our retry logic handled the 429.

O agente executa estes comandos:

apidog import --project <projectId> --format openapi --file ./email-providers.yaml
apidog endpoint list --project <projectId>
apidog environment list --project <projectId>
apidog run --project <projectId> -t <scenarioId> -e <environmentId> \
  --env-var "CF_API_TOKEN=<token>" --env-var "RESEND_API_KEY=<key>" -r cli,junit

Aponte o cenário para endereços verificados na Cloudflare e para o endereço de teste delivered@resend.dev da Resend, para que nenhum teste envie e-mail a um cliente. Adicione --upload-report para ver a execução no app; Apidog CLI no Claude Code cobre a configuração do agente.

Depois que isso funcionar para um desenvolvedor, a equipe pode distribuir a tarefa: o Sharkly é um board onde você atribui tarefas como "migre o e-mail de redefinição de senha para a Cloudflare e execute novamente os testes de e-mail" a agentes de programação que rodam nas suas próprias máquinas com o seu próprio plano do Claude Code, Codex ou OpenCode, executam vários em paralelo e revisam o que entregam antes do merge. É grátis para começar.

Perguntas frequentes

O Cloudflare Email Service é gratuito? Enviar para endereços de destino verificados na sua conta é gratuito em todos os planos, incluindo o Workers Free, e não conta para nenhuma cota. Enviar para qualquer outra pessoa exige o Workers Paid, que inclui 3.000 e-mails por mês e depois custa US$ 0,35 por 1.000.

A Cloudflare é mais barata que a Resend? Na maioria dos volumes, sim. Em 1 milhão de e-mails por mês, é cerca de US$ 354 contra US$ 650. Exatamente nas faixas Pro de 50.000 e 100.000 da Resend, a Resend é alguns dólares mais barata, e abaixo de 3.000 por mês o Resend Free não custa nada.

Posso usar o Cloudflare Email Service sem o Workers? Sim. A API REST e o SMTP funcionam a partir de qualquer backend, mas seu domínio precisa estar na sua conta Cloudflare.

O Cloudflare Email Service rastreia aberturas e cliques? A lista de eventos do Email Sending cobre delivered, deferred, bounced, failed, rejected e complained. Não há eventos de abertura ou clique. A Resend rastreia aberturas e cliques em todos os planos.

Qual é o limite do plano gratuito da Resend? 3.000 e-mails por mês e 100 por dia, 3 domínios e 1 endpoint de webhook, com envio para qualquer destinatário.

title: Explainable Deep Learning for Malaria Parasite Detection and Species Differentiation in Thick Blood Smear Images: A Pilot Feasibility Study
description:
arXiv:2611.31855v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Species-level differentiation of Plasmodium falciparum (PF) and P. vivax (PV) determines treatment, yet deep learning detectors rarely test whether their explanations are reliable. In this pilot feasibility study of TRACE-Mal, a research prototype combining YOLOv8n-seg detection and a six-model soft-voting ensemble, we examined whether agreement among three post-hoc explanation methods (Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP) is associated with the correctness of species calls. the study analysed 2,847 parasite crops from 250 thick smears within publicly available Lacuna Malaria Datasets. The model achieved an mAP50 score of 0.79 and the ensemble had a macro F1 of 0.84 (PF recall 0.86; PV recall 0.74). Unadjusted analyses of crops revealed that predictions explained by greather than or equal to 2 methods were more accurate (86.2% vs 78.9%; difference 7.3 percentage points; 95% CI 3.5-11.1) compared to those explained by less than 2 methods. As the number of explanatory methods increased so did prediction accuracy (from 73.8% for no methods to 89.5% for all three methods). When performing a cluster-bootstrap analysis of 60 test images, again there was a positive consensus difference (7.3 percentage points; 95% CI 2.9-11.8). Further, incorporating explanation information into a model's prediction confidence enhanced its error differentiation ability (AUROC 0.024; 95% CI 0.008-0.041). PF and PV parasite crops have distinct morphologies. Although based on one unvalidated public data source, these findings demonstrate proof-of-concept and should not be taken as a measure of diagnostic capability.

title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
description:
arXiv:2611.31579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. It also consistently achieves a lower reconstruction error than all random-rotation-based algorithms such as EDEN, E-RaBitQ, and TurboQuant.

title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
description:
arXiv:2611.31747v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference reroutes among survivors. At 50% expert removal, FN-Prune achieves lower WikiText-2 perplexity than the best published methods on Qwen3, ERNIE, and OLMoE, including a 32% reduction on OLMoE. At the same budget, GSM8K accuracy improves over the best published methods by 7.5 and 7.0 percentage points on Qwen3 and ERNIE, respectively, while multiple-choice gains remain task-dependent.

title: How Do You Split Work Between Rust and Python in an Automation Service?
description:
Short answer

Use Python for the workflow — queues, browsers, APIs, CRMs, and operator tools — and Rust for the tight loop that must be fast, memory-safe, and easy to run as a small binary: parsing, checksums, audio or byte-level work, and CPU-heavy validation. Keep a clear boundary: Python calls a Rust CLI or shared library with structured input and structured output (JSON or a simple binary protocol). Do not rewrite the whole service in Rust, and do not hide a slow Python loop behind a Rust wrapper that still does the heavy work in Python.

Why split the work at all?

A lot of operations automation starts in Python because the ecosystem is strong: Playwright and Selenium, HTTP clients, pandas or openpyxl for lead files, FastAPI for a control panel, and PyQt or a web UI for staff. That is the right default for glue.

The same process often grows a hot path: normalizing tens of thousands of phone numbers, walking every byte of a recording, hashing files, or validating records before they hit a CRM. Python can do all of that, but when that loop is tight and well-defined, Rust is a good fit: one compiled binary, no GIL in the inner loop, and a type system that catches a class of bugs before the job runs unattended.

The useful design is a pipeline, not a rewrite.

A practical boundary

Give each language a job it is good at:

Layer Prefer Examples
Operator UI, job queue, CRM and HTTP APIs Python FastAPI, Playwright, spreadsheet import, webhook handlers
Tight, deterministic transforms Rust E.164-style digit normalization, file hashing, CSV field cleaning, codec or DSP work
Glue between them A stable contract argv + stdin/stdout JSON, or a cffi / PyO3 module with a small API

Rules that keep the split honest:

  • The Rust side should not open the CRM, the browser, or the mailbox. It should not know about API tokens.
  • The Python side should not reimplement the inner loop “just this once.” If the contract exists, call it.
  • Input and output must be documented and tested from both sides (a fixture file is enough).

A minimal contract: Python calls a Rust CLI

A command-line tool is the simplest boundary. It is easy to test, easy to log, and easy to replace later with a library if you need to.

Rust (concept sketch):

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::io::{self, Read};

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct InRec { phone: Option<String>, email: Option<String> }

#[derive(Serialize)]
struct OutRec {
    phone_e164: Option<String>,
    email: Option<String>,
    ok: bool,
    error: Option<String>,
}

fn normalize_us_phone(raw: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let digits: String = raw.chars().filter(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
    let digits = if digits.len() == 10 {
        format!("1{digits}")
    } else {
        digits
    };
    if digits.len() == 11 && digits.starts_with('1') {
        Some(format!("+{digits}"))
    } else {
        None
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut buf = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut buf)?;
    let rows: Vec<InRec> = serde_json::from_str(&buf)?;
    let out: Vec<OutRec> = rows
        .into_iter()
        .map(|r| {
            let email = r
                .email
                .map(|e| e.trim().to_lowercase())
                .filter(|e| e.contains('@'));
            let phone_e164 = r.phone.as_deref().and_then(normalize_us_phone);
            let ok = email.is_some() || phone_e164.is_some();
            OutRec {
                phone_e164,
                email,
                ok,
                error: if ok { None } else { Some("no valid email or phone".into()) },
            }
        })
        .collect();
    serde_json::to_writer(io::stdout(), &out)?;
    Ok(())
}

Python:

import json, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path

BIN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "bin" / "normalize"

def normalize_batch(records: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [str(BIN)],
        input=json.dumps(records).encode(),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        timeout=30,
        check=False,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(proc.stderr.decode()[:500])
    return json.loads(proc.stdout)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    rows = [{"phone": "(312) 555-0199", "email": "Ops@Example.COM"}]
    print(json.dumps(normalize_batch(rows), indent=2))

Ship a .env.example, never a secret, and keep the Rust binary path configurable. In production, log the Rust exit code and a hash of the input batch, not the raw personal data, unless your retention policy allows it.

When a library is better than a CLI

A CLI is enough for batch jobs. If Python must call the Rust code thousands of times per second inside one process, a PyO3 extension or a small FFI module avoids process startup. Keep the exported API as small as the CLI contract: one function in, one struct out. Do not leak Rust types into the rest of the Python app.

How to test the seam

  • Fixture JSON in, fixture JSON out. Run it from Rust unit tests and from a Python test that shells out to the same binary.
  • Fail closed: malformed JSON, empty stdin, or a non-zero exit must stop the job, not skip records silently.
  • Time the batch on a realistic file size on your machine if you need to decide whether the split is worth it. Do not publish invented speedups.

FAQ

Should every automation project use Rust and Python together?

No. If the work is mostly waiting on a browser, an HTTP API, or a human, Python alone is simpler and easier to hire for. Add Rust when you have a tight, well-specified loop that you will run often.

Is this the same as rewriting the service in Rust?

No. The service stays a Python application. Rust is a dependency for one job, the way you might already call ffmpeg or a Go verifier.

How do I deploy both parts?

Build the Rust binary in CI for the target OS (for example x86_64-pc-windows-msvc or x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu), attach it to the release, and have Python look it up from a known bin/ path. Pin the binary version next to the Python package version.

What about the GIL?

A separate Rust process does not hold the Python GIL. A PyO3 module can release the GIL around the tight loop; do that if you stay in-process and you actually run threads.

Can I put API keys in the Rust binary?

No. Keep secrets in the environment or a secret store on the host. The Rust tool should only see the data it needs to transform.

What this is not

This article does not claim production benchmarks, client results, or a required rewrite of any named product. It is an architecture pattern for Rust & Python automation services.

Written by Muhammad Afzal, a Rust & Python automation engineer at INDUS Web Agency in Islamabad.

title: JetDiffusion: Pushing the Speed Limits of Video Generation with NVFP4 Sparse Attention
description:
arXiv:2611.33268v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attention over long sequences is a major computational bottleneck in video generation, which can be alleviated through sparsity and low-bit quantization. We propose JetDiffusion, a video generation system built on trainable Video Sparse Quantized Attention (VSQA), with custom inference kernels that combine native NVFP4 computation and kernel fusion. At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8-29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares. To further accelerate video generation, we combine VSQA with NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation. Although each technique can individually preserve generation quality, jointly adapting to all three remains challenging, particularly under aggressive NVFP4 quantization. Through empirical studies, we develop an effective staged training recipe that enables stable adaptation to quantization, sparsity, and few-step denoising. On Wan2.1-14B, the resulting model achieves 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 while maintaining comparable video quality.
